Subject: Re: Order form — service credit matrix + next steps for legal review

Aisha — thanks for the matrix. We reviewed internally and have three items we'd like clarified before we send this to procurement:

1) Maintenance blackout windows: your order form lists a single 4-hour weekly maintenance window. BrightSail policy requires a maximum of 2 hours per weekly window and advance notice of 5 business days for non-emergency maintenance. Can you confirm if Redwood can support that?

2) Uptime calculation: please confirm whether downtime is measured at the region level or per-customer node. Our infra team wants deterministic SLAs for the us-east-1 region.

3) Credit caps: we can't accept unlimited credits; will Redwood accept a quarterly cap (e.g., 100% of monthly committed spend) rather than an open-ended liability?

We attached our annotated redlines (BrightSail_OrderForm_Redlines_20280311.pdf). Happy to jump on a short call if needed.

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Procurement, BrightSail

Tara — great questions. Quick responses inline below, and I've attached a proposed credit matrix that maps to three uptime tiers. I can also sync with your counsel if helpful.

1) Maintenance blackout windows — we can revise the order form to allow a 2-hour weekly window with 5 business days notice for non-emergency maintenance. For emergency security patches we'll keep the current emergency exception language (we'll provide post-event report).

2) Uptime calculation — Redwood measures availability at the tenant level by default. For BrightSail we can provide region-level availability reporting for us-east-1 and an SLA that references region-level metrics. That will require enabling region-affinity on the dedicated pool but is doable.

3) Credit caps — we are open to a quarterly cap. Proposed compromise: cap credits at 125% of quarterly committed spend; we can push to 100% after legal review if BrightSail requires.

Next steps:
- I've uploaded Redwood_SLA_Credit_Matrix_v3.xlsx to the Drive link below and attached a PDF summary.
- Marissa will coordinate with legal on final wording for the maintenance and cap language.
- If BrightSail counsel wants a line-by-line redline review, Steph can join a call Thursday or Friday.

Proposed times: Thu 3/13 09:00–10:00 PT or Fri 3/14 13:00–14:00 PT. Which works?

Aisha Rahman

Hi Tara / Michael — thanks for the specifics. Per Aisha's note, our proposed edits are below and I'll have Redwood legal prepare the line edits for your counsel to review:

- Maintenance window: revise to a maximum 2-hour weekly window with 5 business days advance notice. Add a separate clause for emergency maintenance with post-event report.
- Non-emergency small patches: add language requiring 24-hour notice and limit the total number of such patches to 4 per quarter (to address operational churn).
- Uptime calc: define "Region Availability" as the percentage of 5-minute measurement intervals in us-east-1 reporting healthy for customer workloads; include a reporting export to BrightSail on request.
- Credit cap: propose quarterly cap at 110% of committed quarterly spend. This is our middle ground between your ask and our prior 125% suggestion.

I'll circulate a tracked-redline PDF by end of day Wednesday. If you prefer a live session to walk through the redlines, Steph and I can lead the review.

Thanks,

Marissa / Aisha — BrightLaw reviewed Redwood's proposal. A few redline items from counsel:

1) Emergency maintenance carve-out: suggest adding a requirement that Redwood provide an initial incident summary within 24 hours and a full RCA within 7 business days for any emergency maintenance that results in customer-impacting downtime.

2) Credit calculation: BrightLaw requests explicit formula language. Recommended: "Service Credit = (Committed Monthly Fee) * (Downtime% beyond SLA threshold) * (Prorated factor per schedule)" — we'll send exact phrasing.

3) Cap language: counsel prefers the 100% quarterly cap but can accept 110% if Redwood adds a reciprocal limitation on BrightSail-requested high-frequency testing that could artificially inflate observed downtime (i.e., agreed test windows).

We can take the redline call tomorrow at 09:00 PT. Please confirm and send the tracked PDF.

Ellie Chan
Counsel, BrightLaw (on behalf of BrightSail)
